newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate committee passes PUHCA repeal bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate committee passes PUHCA repeal bill.

text.p: The U.S. Senate Banking Committee Thursday passed a bill to repeal the Public Utility Holding Company Act (PUHCA) but give federal and state energy regulators more authority to monitor utility investments to protect electric consumers.

The 1935 law, which controls holding companies which have utilities in more than one state, was designed to protect shareholders from subsidizing electric utilities' unprofitable attempts to diversify into unrelated businesses.

The eleven electric and three gas utilities which are registered holding companies want the law repealed so that they can invest in other businesses without having to seek approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission.

"It's more than important (to us). It's an emergency," said E.R. (Dick) Brooks, CEO of Central and South West Corp, adding that because SEC approvals often took months, the law limited the company's ability to compete against companies not subject to the act.
The SEC itself has said the holding company act is obsolete and redundant, because the protections it provides are duplicated by state and federal utility commissions.
"The goal of PUHCA reform is to increase competition so that consumers ultimately pay lower utility rates, not higher rates," said Banking Committee chairman Sen. Alfonse D'Amato.
D'Amato told reporters he expected the full Senate to vote on the bill before Congress's August recess, and PUHCA repeal advocates said they were optimistic that the bill would pass.
"There's a high degree of sympathy in the House and the Senate for repeal," Brooks told reporters.

However, he said passage on the House side would be more difficult, because Republican leaders pushing to deregulate local power markets and senior House Democrats want to repeal PUHCA only as part of a broad electric restructuring bill.

Sen. Richard Bryan, a Nevada Democrat who voted against the bill, warned that consumers were concerned that without local power market competition in place, PUHCA repeal "could ... create a situation where there is a concentration in the marketplace that could ultimately be counterproductive."
The holding companies account for about $100 billion worth, or 20 percent of all the electric utility assets owned by investor-owned utilities.

The companies affected include: Allegheny Power System Inc, American Electric Power Co Inc, Central and South West, Cinergy, Eastern Utilities Associates, Entergy Corp, General Public Utilities Corp, New England Electric System, Northeast Utilities, Southern Co, Unitil Corp, Columbia Gas System, Consolidated Natural Gas Co, and National Fuels Gas Co.
